note: Placed pieces (docs 09, docs/future/10; src/world/pieces): objects that rest on the ground rather than being part of it. The first is the loose stone, the naturalist's reward at six finds (naturalist.json). cap: how many loose stones an island may hold; at the cap the Loose stone mode says so calmly and sets no more. sizeM: a stone's length in meters [min, max], picked by its seed. sink: the share of a stone's height set into the ground, so it sits rather than rests. lean: how much of the ground's slope a stone leans with (0 level, 1 flat on the slope). grassClear: blades stand no nearer a stone's middle than this share of its half length (src/render/passes/grass.js clears), so it sits in the grass rather than the grass growing through it. tapM and tapPerM: how near a tap must be to pick a stone (plus this much per meter of camera distance; never less than about half the stone's length). arrive: when the reward is given, count stones come by themselves on grounds (painted grass or soil) between nearM [min, max] meters from fresh water (a pond or stream, never the sea or a damp hollow), never in water, on ground no steeper than maxSlope (rise over run across a meter), at least spacingM apart; placed from the world seed, so live play and catch-up give the same stones. tip: a tap on a stone lifts its near edge by tipDeg over tipS seconds (pivoting on the far edge, so you see underneath), holds for holdS, then settles back over settleS. shape: the stones are baked from blended ellipsoids (src/world/creatures/body-bake.js): count shapes, seeded from seed; widthShare and heightShare [min, max] of the length; lobes extra lumps blended in by blendM; cellM the bake grid; then cut by facets: a top plane tilted up to topTilt and cutting at topShare [min, max] of the stone's reach upward (a flatter top), and chips planes round the shoulders, rising chipUp [min, max] and cutting at chipShare of the reach that way. albedo: weathered grey stone (linear, darker than fresh rock, in the island rock's own hue); underside: damp and soil-stained where it lies in the ground; mottle: broad and fine tone wander (shares) at broadPerUnit and finePerUnit waves per mesh unit, and hue a touch warmer or cooler with the broad patches. The draw pass (src/shaders/piece-draw.wgsl) lays the island's scanned rock over this, triplanar in the stone's frame: its variation about the rock's mean (terrain.json albedoRock), its normals (look.normalStrength) and roughness. Albedos are physical; the palette paints at tonemap (docs/05). damp: the dark patch the stone leaves on the ground, as a share of its footprint (scale), with its albedo at the middle and edge (linear). ring: the soft damp darkening of the ground round each stone's foot: darkness 0..1, scale over the footprint. words: the Loose stone mode's calm lines (full at the cap, water when a tap lands in water).

words.full: The island holds all the loose stones it can for now. Remove one to set it somewhere else.
words.water: A loose stone sits on land. Tap the ground.

driftwoodNote: Driftwood (docs 13, docs/future/10; src/world/pieces/driftwood.js), the naturalist's reward at ten finds. Once given, each high tide may leave logs on its strandline (shore.json look.strandline): only the newest lines keep logs (lines), each tide perTide [min, max] logs, at most most on the island at once; a log lies on dry or damp ground within bandReachM of the sea's tide band (never a pond's bank), where the ground is within lineToleranceM of the line's reach and both its ends within endToleranceM, on ground no steeper than maxSlope, along the shore give or take yawJitterDeg, at least spacingM apart. Seeded from the world seed and the tide, so nothing is saved: a later tide that sweeps the line takes its logs. lengthM and thickM [min, max]: a log's size in meters. sink: the share of its thickness set into the sand; lean: how much of the slope it leans with. grassClear: blades stand no nearer than its half thickness plus grassClearM, in circles along its length. tapReachM: a tap picks a log within its half thickness and this much of its line (a tap on a low log's top lands on the sand behind it). ringHalf: the damp ring's half width and half length as shares of its footprint. roll: a tap rolls it rollDeg away from you over tipS, holds holdS, and rolls back over settleS, showing the damp sand where it lay (damp: that patch's albedos, linear). forms (L2, src/world/pieces/log-bake.js): every log is baked from its own seed in one of four forms, picked by weights (straight trunk, bowed limb, forked branch, root end); each form's bow (sideways, in thicknesses) and taper [min, max] (a share of its radius); a bowed limb gets extraStubs more stubs; a forked branch's snapped arm leaves the trunk at [min, max] of its length, angleDeg off it, armLength [min, max] of the log's length, armRadius of the trunk's radius there; a root end flares by flare [min, max] over its first flareShare of its length, with roots [min, max] broken roots splaying out and backShare back along it, length [min, max] and radius [min, max] in thicknesses. stub: count [min, max] snapped side stubs, radius a share of the trunk's radius, length in thicknesses, leaning up to leanDeg toward the far end. Each end splits with splitChance: a crack splitDeep [min, max] thicknesses in, pinched in by splitPinch. sea: how long a log drifted comes from its seed too, 0 fresh to 1 old, leaning old by leanOld (a power); old logs' broken ends are worn round by wearEnds. age (src/world/pieces/log-age.js): a kept log ages where it lies, from startDays to fullDays after it was set down, darkening by darken (a share of its tone) and its cracks and grain softening by soften; worked out from the world, never saved. Its ground is damp under a damp hollow, or near fresh water (full within damp.fullM, none past nearM); shaded by tall plants within shade.radiusM (plants: each kind's weight times its size, full shade at full), or by a bank rising more than bankM at bankAtM on several sides (worth bank). moss: in damp shade (where [from, to] of the two together) moss creeps over its top from startDays to fullDays, up to most; drawn in the stepping stones' moss albedo. refreshS: how often (real seconds) a kept log's damp and shade are looked at again. look: barkAlbedo (linear) and barkCover, the share of a fresh log still in bark; shipwormDarkness the old wood's grooves; oldCrackWidth how far the oldest wood's checking cracks open. shape: each log around vertices round and rings along; swell a gentle unevenness, knots [min, max] of knotSize [min, max] (shares of its length) rising knotRise; jag how far the broken ends are torn back (share of its length). albedo: sea-weathered silver-grey (linear), endAlbedo the end grain, knotAlbedo round the knots, underside where it lies in the damp sand below stainLine (a share of its thickness); mottle: broad and fine tone along its length. look (piece-draw.wgsl): roughness, bumpM the grain and cracks' relief, grainAcross streaks across the log, crackDarkness 0..1. cap: how many logs an island keeps (apart from the stones' cap). carry: the turtles' gift (unlocks.carry, or ?sandbox, or ?driftwood): a carried piece hangs liftM above its spot until set down.
steppingNote: Stepping stones and the treads of Steps (docs 09; src/world/pieces/slabs.js): each is one of a small library of rounded slab shapes, 1 mesh unit long, that the draw pass scales and turns. slab: count shapes, seeded from seed, each around vertices round, with topRings rings across its top and bevelRows rows round its rounded edge. The footprint is a rounded rectangle (a superellipse): widthShare [min, max] is its width as a share of its length, power [min, max] how square its corners are (2 an oval, higher squarer), and its outline wobbles by wobble (a share) in wobbleHarmonics [min, max] gentle waves round it. The top is nearly flat: domeShare [min, max] how much it rises in the middle (share of the length), tiltDeg [min, max] how far it leans; bevelShare [min, max] the radius of the rounded edge; capShare [min, max] how thick the stone looks (how far below the top the sides turn straight down), the sides widening by batterShare over that depth and lumpy by lump (a share). skirtUnits: how far the sides go on down below that (in lengths), so a stone can stand on a deep pond bed; the draw pass sinks what is not needed into the ground. albedo: weathered grey stone (linear); underside: the stained tone the sides reach more than stainUnits (in lengths) below the top's lowest edge; topLift: how much lighter the top is, topSmooth how much of the fine grain it loses; mottle: broad and fine tone wander (shares) at broadPerUnit and finePerUnit waves per mesh unit, and hue a touch warmer or cooler with the broad patches. Albedos are physical; the palette paints at tonemap (docs/05). Pond stones (src/world/pieces/stepping.js; Sculpt's Pond stones mode): cap how many an island holds. A drag lays one every spacingM [min, max] (seeded) along it, nudged up to jitterM to the side, never nearer than apartM to another stone; a line stops where the water is deeper than maxDepthM. Water deeper than wetM counts: there a stone is sizeM [min, max] long plus growPerM for each metre of depth, and stands its top freeboardM [min, max] above the water as it is when laid; on land its top is landRiseM [min, max] above the ground, and it leans with the slope by lean. linkM and stepM: any two stones no further apart than linkM, whose tops differ by no more than stepM, are one way across for the walker, both ways and whichever line each was laid in, footing within footReachM of the line between them. wadeM: as deep as the walker can wade (walker.json grid.wadeM); a stone standing in deeper water is laid only where the walker can step back from it, to another stone or to ground it can stand on, else the line stops with the gap line. moss: from startDays to fullDays after it was laid, moss grows on its rounded edge up to most (0..1), creeping over the top by band; albedo linear. sitInsetM: how far in from its edge a creature sits. words: the mode's calm lines.

words.full: The island holds all the pond stones it can for now. Remove some to lay them somewhere else.
words.deep: The water is too deep here for a stone to stand. Try nearer the edge.
words.gap: That stone would be too far to step back from. Start the line from the bank or from a stone.
words.hint: Drag across shallow water to lay a line of stones, or click for one. Click a stone to select it.

raftNote: The reed raft (the turtles' gift, unlocks.raft; src/world/pieces/raft.js): the Water tool's Raft mode sets one where you tap open fresh water. cap: how many an island holds. sizeM [min, max]: its length (m), from its seed. It goes only where the water is at least minDepthM deep under its middle and at least rimDepthM toward its rim (away from the bank), never in the sea, at least apartM from another raft or stone. It floats with its base draftM under the water as it is now (so its top stands a few centimetres proud), bobbing by bobM over bobS seconds, easing to a new level over settleS; where the water has gone it rests on the ground. sitInsetM: how far in from its edge a creature sits. shape: count shapes from seed, each bundles reed bundles across widthShare [min, max] of its length, around vertices round and rings along; fatten swells them to touch, round shortens the outer ones (rounded corners), taper how far from each end they thin; bands ties at bandM wide, pinching by pinch and darker by bandDark; streak the reed stems along each bundle; albedo dry straw and endAlbedo the cut ends (linear; the palette paints at tonemap). words: the Raft mode's calm lines.

words.hint: Click open water to set a reed raft. Click a raft to select it.
words.full: The island holds all the rafts it can for now. Remove one to set it somewhere else.
words.shallow: A raft needs open water, deeper than your knees and away from the bank.
words.sea: A raft rests on fresh water, not the sea.
words.near: That is too near another raft or stone. Try a little further out.

lanternNote: The lantern (B2 L1, Matt, October 30, 2026; src/world/pieces/lantern.js and lantern-live.js): a placed piece of kind 'lantern', the shaper's trail's gift for a pond of your own with no fish, made at the workbench (cook.json post-lantern) and set down from its pouch's card (Set it here, on foot: setAheadM in front of you, turning up to setTurnDeg from the view to find a spot, on dry land off the camp ground, at least apartM from another). It stays where it is set and lights itself every dusk, with no fuel and nothing to tend, whether you are near or away: from litAtSunDeg of sun altitude it brightens, full by fullAtSunDeg, and goes out the same way at dawn (worked out from the clock, never saved). cap: how many lanterns the island holds, counting any in the pack or still being made (one now; three once M3's paths come). sizeM: its footprint (the grass clear and the carry ring). post: a stick post heightM above the ground and sinkM into it, radiusM at the foot thinning to topRadiusM, a rush tie bandM wide at bandAtM of its height; pot: the clay housing sitting on its top, radiusM round its widest and heightM tall, pierced by rows rows of holes (holeM across) the light shows through, a lid knob knobM; each drawn in one colour (srgb, rough; the props pass, src/render/passes/props.js); the post leans up to leanDeg by its seed. light: its point light at the pot's middle (lightK kelvin, cd candela, reaching rangeM, flicker share at flickerHz; doc 06 Lanterns and small lights), drawn among the small lights after the camp's own; glass: the glow seen through its holes (nits, m across; camp-fx.wgsl, as the hand lantern's glass), drawn nearShare of the pot's radius toward the eye so the pot does not hide it, and moths circle it after dark. tapM: how near a tap must land for its card; reachM: within this of it on foot, Take up puts it back in the pack. words: its card and the pouch card's calm lines.

lantern.micaNote: The mica lantern (the pan finds): mica in its holes makes its light this much brighter (cd), its flicker this share of a plain lantern's, and warmer (rgb, linear, luminance about 1 is not kept: it tints).

words.name: Lantern
words.lit: A clay lantern on its post, lit for the night. It needs nothing from you.
words.dark: A clay lantern on its post. It wakes by itself at dusk.
words.set: Set down. It will light itself at dusk.
words.where: Not here. A lantern stands on dry ground, away from the camp and from another lantern.
words.full: The island has all the lanterns it can keep for now.
words.far: Go a little closer to take it up.
words.noRoom: No room in the pack for the lantern.
words.moved: Set down here. It lights itself at dusk, wherever it stands.

stepsNote: Steps (doc 13, the shaper's trail; src/world/pieces/steps.js): a flight cut between two levels of ground, dragged from one to the other. widthM: how wide a flight is (wide enough that the walker's half-metre grid always finds a level way up its middle). Every rise is at most maxRiseM and every tread at least minTreadM and at most maxTreadM, and the whole flight rises no steeper than maxPitch (rise over run), so the walker can always climb it; a drag shorter than that asks for more. minDropM: the least difference in level worth a step. landM: how far the flight runs on past each end at that end's level, so it meets the ground. cap: how many flights an island holds. rockShare: how far toward rock the flight's cells and the sheer walls beside it (any drop over faceDropM to a neighbour) are painted. slab: perTread slabs side by side on each tread, filling fill of their share (the rest is the gaps between them), turned up to yawJitterDeg off square, their tops riseM over the tread, with a skirt skirtUnits deep (lengths; short, since a flight can stand out from the slope). words: the Steps mode's calm lines.

words.hint: Drag from a terrace down to the ground below to cut a flight of steps. Click a flight to select it.
words.flat: These two places are at the same level. Start on a terrace and drag down to the ground below it.
words.short: That is too steep for steps. Drag a little further, about {m} m in all.
words.overlap: Steps are already cut here. Remove them first to cut new ones.
words.full: The island holds all the flights of steps it can for now.
words.water: Steps start and end on dry ground.
